title: Vintage Gibson SG Junior Value Guide: Finish And Era
description: Understand vintage SG Junior value through its era, original P-90, finish and repair history. Joe explains what to compare before selling a one-pickup SG.
h1: Vintage Gibson SG Junior Value Guide
alt: Cherry Gibson SG Junior with one black dog-ear P-90 pickup, two knobs and a wraparound bridge

faqs.q: How Much Is A Vintage Gibson SG Junior Worth?
faqs.a: A cherry 1962 to 1964 Gibson SG Junior with its original finish and P-90, original case and minor parts changes falls around $6,000 to $8,500 as of October 2026. That comparison allows a replacement guard or bridge and doesn't establish the price of an untouched collector example.

faqs.q: What Condition Does This Price Range Assume?
faqs.a: Original finish and P-90, original case, no reported structural repair. Allows replacement pickguard or bridge with original part retained, or added shielding. Not an untouched collector band. I match those details before using the $6,000 to $8,500 range for an individual guitar.

faqs.q: Is A Dealer Offer The Same As The Published Range?
faqs.a: It isn't. The table describes completed-sale comparisons before shipping and tax. A buying offer also accounts for the instrument's condition, selling costs, preparation and the dealer's margin. I explain an offer for the actual guitar rather than promising the top of a general range.

faqs.q: Does A Quality Refret Change The Collector Category?
faqs.a: A quality refret is accepted maintenance and preserves the all-original classification of an otherwise all-original guitar. It takes the instrument out of the museum-quality category. Neck reshaping is a separate alteration.
